evidence.positive: On the running mayo-mayo tenant (local, build c45154016), staged a patient with a p-cystoscopy case (pathway SULFAMETHOXAZOLE_TRIMETHOPRIM_PO -> CEFAZOLIN). Added an allergy coded SNOMED 372788003 via POST /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/allergies?type=SNOMED (runs the same AllergyAssociationService.associateAllergiesViaRxNormMapping the Mayo FHIR ingestion calls). Observed: patient_medication_allergies gained a row with category SULFONAMIDE; GET .../antibiotic-candidates returned outcome=RECOMMENDED recommended=[CEFAZOLIN] (log: Category SULFAMETHOXAZOLE_TRIMETHOPRIM_PO ruled out by rule a-general-allergy); POST /api/cds/medication-selection with m-cefazolin as loopuser returned rules fired=[w-default-dose-adjustment] only, and /api/admin/rule/evaluations/not-fired recorded a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic with explanation "Selected medication is a preferred antibiotic candidate". Repeated on a second patient with the SMX-TMP combination RxNorm code 10831: same SULFONAMIDE medication allergy, CEFAZOLIN recommended, wrong-antibiotic abstained. Backfill (changeset 231): the shipped SQL was re-run by hand against mayo-mayo after setting the two real alert-compliance rows to compliant=false; the row for the firing whose 372788003 allergy predated it and whose selected drug (cefazolin) is the fallback step flipped to compliant=true (UPDATE 1). The changeset shows EXECUTED in mayo-mayo and MARK_RAN in demo-demo, confirming the Mayo-only guard.
evidence.negative: Same case shape with no sulfa allergy on record: candidates returned recommended=[SULFAMETHOXAZOLE_TRIMETHOPRIM_PO] and selecting m-cefazolin fired a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic (resultId 01a10d14-42c2-..., ALTERNATIVE_ANTIBIOTIC_CANDIDATES = SMX-TMP step 1), so the alert still fires when the allergy is genuinely absent. With the recognized sulfa allergy, selecting the sulfa tablet itself fired a-general-allergy and wrong-antibiotic abstained with "Selected medication was ruled out for this patient", so recognition cuts both ways. The backfill left the compliance row of that no-allergy-at-firing-time firing at compliant=false (allergy created after fired_at), i.e. it did not over-mark.
evidence.red_check: Data flip to the pre-fix state: deleted the SNOMED 372788003 row from mayo-mayo allergy_cross_reaction_group_snomed_codes (DELETE 1, count 0). Added the identical 372788003 allergy to a fresh third patient (RedCheck, operation 01a10d15-32c8-702e-b1e6-5f1b44c20f07): patient_allergies=1, patient_medication_allergies=0; candidates went back to recommended=[SULFAMETHOXAZOLE_TRIMETHOPRIM_PO]; selecting m-cefazolin fired a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic (resultId 01a10d15-a1ed-...), and the app log printed the RuleEngine line for that operation with -> true (the signature). Reverted: reinserted the row (SULFONAMIDE|372788003), deleted and re-added the patient allergy, which now produced the SULFONAMIDE medication allergy; candidates=[CEFAZOLIN], selection fired only w-default-dose-adjustment, and the log line for the same operation reads -> false Selected medication is a preferred antibiotic candidate. The signature appears exactly once in the full container log.

caveats: Allergies were injected through the admin allergies endpoint, which calls the same association method as MayoGetPatientInfoStrategy but bypasses the RXNORM_ALLERGY_MAPPING flag check and Epic AllergyIntolerance parsing; real Mayo FHIR ingestion is unreachable here. Earlier sessions concluded the flag is on for mayo-mayo in prod (Jordan's firings), not re-verified now.

Changeset 231 was validated by re-running its SQL by hand against real firings with compliance set to false by SQL; Liquibase itself ran it once at boot on an empty schema. Production runs it once against real history.
Only SNOMED 372788003 and RxNorm 10831 were exercised at runtime; the other eight added codes are present in the DB group (18 RxNorm, 2 SNOMED) and pinned by AllergyCrossReactionGroupCSVImporterTest.
The ticket also asks to mark the firings in the Sprint 93 SharePoint document as compliant; that document is outside this environment.
Alert-compliance rows are written compliant=true at firing time here; the production false verdicts the backfill targets come from a later evaluator step not exercised in this run.

automation.assessment: AllergyCrossReactionGroupCSVImporterTest already pins all ten new codes to the SULFONAMIDE group, and AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest covers a cross-reaction-group allergy ruling out the step, but only via an RxNorm-coded allergy with a synthetic group. Nothing covers a SNOMED-coded class allergy walking into the fallback, nor the wrong-antibiotic rule abstaining for cefazolin on the SMX-TMP -> CEFAZOLIN pathway when the patient is sulfa-allergic. The demo tenant has no sulfonamide pathway, so this is backend-test territory, not qa-suite.
proposed_tests: AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest: a SNOMED-coded allergy (372788003) in the SULFONAMIDE cross-reaction group rules out the SULFAMETHOXAZOLE_TRIMETHOPRIM_PO step and the walk recommends CEFAZOLIN (mirror of the existing RxNorm-coded case).

ProcedureBasedWrongAntibioticRule test: sulfa-allergic patient on a SMX-TMP -> CEFAZOLIN pathway selecting cefazolin abstains with "Selected medication is a preferred antibiotic candidate"; same patient without the allergy fires with SMX-TMP as the alternative.
AllergyAssociationServiceTest: SNOMED 372788003 and RxNorm 10831 each produce a single SULFONAMIDE category MedicationAllergy (and no duplicate when both codes arrive on the same patient).

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A Mayo cystoscopy case with a sulfa allergy coded SNOMED 372788003 (and separately RxNorm 10831) now yields a SULFONAMIDE medication allergy, cefazolin becomes the recommended antibiotic, and selecting cefazolin no longer fires a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic.
Negative: The same case with no sulfa allergy still recommends SMX-TMP and still fires the wrong-antibiotic alert on cefazolin.
Red check: Removing 372788003 from the SULFONAMIDE group in the database made a freshly added sulfa allergy go unrecognized and the alert fired again on cefazolin; restoring the row made it abstain.

Backfill: The changeset 231 SQL run by hand against real firings marked compliant only the firing whose coded sulfa allergy predated it and whose selected drug was the fallback step.

Automation: Proposed a SNOMED-coded variant in the pathway spec test and a wrong-antibiotic rule test for the sulfa-allergic cefazolin selection.
